Definition
[Orbifold atlas] \group foundations Source: thurston:page-0318, thurston:page-0319

An $n$-orbifold is a Hausdorff space $X_O$ covered by open sets $U_i$ closed under finite intersections, with charts $U_i\cong \widetilde U_i/\Gamma _i$, where $\widetilde U_i\subset \mathbb R^n$ is open and $\Gamma _i$ is finite. For $U_i\subset U_j$ there are an injective homomorphism $f_{ij}:\Gamma _i\hookrightarrow \Gamma _j$ and an equivariant embedding $\widetilde\varphi _{ij}:\widetilde U_i\hookrightarrow \widetilde U_j$. These data are defined up to the natural action of $\Gamma _j$; on triple overlaps the two composites agree up to conjugacy.
Proof

\sketch The quotient maps give the local models. Restriction of a chart to a smaller chart induces the injective isotropy map and equivariant lift; changing the lift changes both maps by an element of the larger isotropy group.

□
